steps.message:
# RL training run diagnosis

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a historical snapshot: inspect its source,
effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic, logs,
tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Do not assume that an unusual
setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed behavior.

Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime,
optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish
held-out health. A truncated log is not by itself proof of a defect.

Do not launch a full training run, use the network, or modify the historical
snapshot. The dataset, held-out set, model, training-step budget, and evaluation
interval are fixed.

## Deliverable

Write one concise UTF-8 diagnosis to:

```text
$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/agent_answer.md
```

State the verdict, identify the concrete root cause or causes, and explain the
causal chain using specific workspace evidence. Distinguish root causes from
symptoms. Do not propose or implement a fix, and do not write other deliverable
files.
Exploring the workspace structure before forming any conclusions.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# GRPO | Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct | GSM8K train 7,473 / GSM8K test 1,319 held-out | FSDP + vLLM | 1 GPU
#
# verl GSM8K GRPO quickstart recipe, scaled to one GPU, with the MATH-style prompt from
# examples/data_preprocess/gsm8k_boxed.py ('... output the final answer within \\boxed{}.'). The reward
# is Math-Verify through verl's built-in scorer (rewards/math_verify_reward.py, wired in with
# reward.custom_reward_function); verl uses the same function for the held-out metric
# val-core/openai/gsm8k/acc/mean@1 on the full GSM8K test split (greedy).
#
# trainer.use_v1=False selects the verl/trainer/ppo/ray_trainer.py loop; the v1 trainer needs
# the optional TransferQueue package, which is not installed.
#
# Everything the run writes goes to $LOG_DIR:
#   train.log                       full stdout/stderr of the trainer
#   metrics.jsonl                   one JSON line per training step (verl file logger)
#   wandb/                          offline W&B run
#   rollouts/<step>.jsonl           training rollouts (prompt, response, score) per step
#   val_generations/<step>.jsonl    held-out generations at each evaluation
#   rollouts/ and val_generations/ carry the score the reward assigned to each response.

set -xeuo pipefail

W=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
cd "$W"

# ---- user-adjustable ----
MODEL_PATH=${MODEL_PATH:-$W/models/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct}
TRAIN_FILE=${TRAIN_FILE:-$W/data/gsm8k_boxed/train.parquet}
VAL_FILE=${VAL_FILE:-$W/data/gsm8k_boxed/test.parquet}
LOG_DIR=${LOG_DIR:-$W/outputs/run}
NGPUS_PER_NODE=${NGPUS_PER_NODE:-1}

TOTAL_STEPS=${TOTAL_STEPS:-100}
TEST_FREQ=${TEST_FREQ:-10}
SEED=${SEED:-42}

TRAIN_BATCH_SIZE=128         # prompts per step
ROLLOUT_N=8                  # responses per prompt (GRPO group size)
PPO_MINI_BATCH_SIZE=4        # smaller mini-batches to fit memory
MAX_PROMPT_LENGTH=512
MAX_RESPONSE_LENGTH=512

ACTOR_LR=2e-6
KL_LOSS_COEF=0.001

PROJECT_NAME=${PROJECT_NAME:-grpo_gsm8k}
EXPERIMENT_NAME=${EXPERIMENT_NAME:-qwen2_5_0_5b_gsm8k_boxed_grpo}
# ---- end user-adjustable ----

if [ ! -f "$MODEL_PATH/config.json" ]; then
    echo "model not found at $MODEL_PATH" >&2; exit 1
fi
if [ ! -f "$TRAIN_FILE" ] || [ ! -f "$VAL_FILE" ]; then
    python3 examples/data_preprocess/gsm8k_boxed.py --local_dataset_path "$W/data/raw/gsm8k" --local_save_dir "$(dirname "$TRAIN_FILE")"
fi

mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
export PYTHONPATH="$W${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"
export WANDB_MODE=${WANDB_MODE:-offline}
export WANDB_DIR=${WANDB_DIR:-$LOG_DIR}
export VERL_FILE_LOGGER_PATH="$LOG_DIR/metrics.jsonl"
export TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false

DATA=(
    algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo
    algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=False
    data.train_files="$TRAIN_FILE"
    data.val_files="$VAL_FILE"
    data.train_batch_size=$TRAIN_BATCH_SIZE
    data.max_prompt_length=$MAX_PROMPT_LENGTH
    data.max_response_length=$MAX_RESPONSE_LENGTH
    data.filter_overlong_prompts=True
    data.truncation=error
    data.seed=$SEED
)

MODEL=(
    actor_rollout_ref.model.path="$MODEL_PATH"
    actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=True
    actor_rollout_ref.model.enable_gradient_checkpointing=True
)

ACTOR=(
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr=$ACTOR_LR
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size=$PPO_MINI_BATCH_SIZE
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz=True
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_max_token_len_per_gpu=24576
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss=True
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_coef=$KL_LOSS_COEF
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_type=low_var_kl
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.entropy_coeff=0
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.loss_agg_mode=token-mean
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.data_loader_seed=$SEED
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.param_offload=False
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.optimizer_offload=False
)

ROLLOUT=(
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.name=vllm
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.tensor_model_parallel_size=1
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.gpu_memory_utilization=0.4
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n=$ROLLOUT_N
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.temperature=1.0
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.top_p=1.0
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.top_k=-1
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.seed=$SEED
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_use_dynamic_bsz=True
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_max_token_len_per_gpu=24576
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.n=1
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.do_sample=False
    actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_use_dynamic_bsz=True
    actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_max_token_len_per_gpu=24576
)

REWARD=(
    reward.custom_reward_function.path="$W/rewards/math_verify_reward.py"
    reward.custom_reward_function.name=compute_score
)

TRAINER=(
    trainer.use_v1=False
    trainer.critic_warmup=0
    trainer.logger='["console","wandb","file"]'
    trainer.project_name=$PROJECT_NAME
    trainer.experiment_name=$EXPERIMENT_NAME
    trainer.n_gpus_per_node=$NGPUS_PER_NODE
    trainer.nnodes=1
    trainer.val_before_train=True
    trainer.test_freq=$TEST_FREQ
    trainer.save_freq=-1
    trainer.total_epochs=100
    trainer.total_training_steps=$TOTAL_STEPS
    trainer.rollout_data_dir="$LOG_DIR/rollouts"
    trainer.validation_data_dir="$LOG_DIR/val_generations"
    trainer.default_local_dir="$LOG_DIR/checkpoints"
)

python3 -m verl.trainer.main_ppo \
    "${DATA[@]}" \
    "${MODEL[@]}" \
    "${ACTOR[@]}" \
    "${ROLLOUT[@]}" \
    "${REWARD[@]}" \
    "${TRAINER[@]}" \
    "$@" 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_DIR/train.log"

"""Reward: Math-Verify equivalence between the response's final answer and the gold answer.

Thin wrapper around verl's built-in scorer ``verl.utils.reward_score.math_verify.compute_score``
(the one verl's ``default_compute_score`` comments suggest for MATH-style data). Wired in through
``reward.custom_reward_function.path/name`` (see run_gsm8k_grpo.sh); verl calls
``compute_score(data_source=..., solution_str=..., ground_truth=..., extra_info=...)`` from its
reward loop and uses the same function for the held-out validation metric.
"""

from verl.utils.reward_score import math_verify


def compute_score(data_source, solution_str, ground_truth, extra_info=None, **kwargs):
    if solution_str is None:
        return 0.0
    return float(math_verify.compute_score(solution_str, str(ground_truth)))

import json

# Analyze all three rollout steps in detail
for f in ['1','50','100']:
    path = f'/workspace/results/run100/rollouts/{f}.jsonl'
    rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open(path)]
    scores = [float(r['score']) for r in rows]
    correct = sum(1 for s in scores if s >= 1.0)
    total = len(rows)
    
    # Count output length distribution
    lens = [len(r['output']) for r in rows]
    short = sum(1 for l in lens if l < 50)
    
    print(f"\n=== Rollout step {f} ===")
    print(f"  total={total}, correct={correct}, acc={correct/total:.3f}")
    print(f"  outputs <50 chars: {short} ({100*short/total:.1f}%)")
    print(f"  avg output len: {sum(lens)/len(lens):.0f} chars")
    
    # Sample wrong and right answers
    wrong = [r for r in rows if float(r['score']) < 1.0][:3]
    right = [r for r in rows if float(r['score']) >= 1.0][:2]
    
    print("  WRONG samples:")
    for r in wrong:
        print(f"    output={r['output'][:200]!r}  gt={r['gts']!r}")
    print("  CORRECT samples:")
    for r in right:
        print(f"    output={r['output'][:200]!r}  gt={r['gts']!r}")
EOF

3. Entropy: starts0.35at step 1, drops to ~0.15-0.25 in middle steps, then EXPLODES to 0.80-0.86 at steps 97-99
4. KL loss: monotonically grows from 0.0026 to 0.29 (100x increase over training)
5. Repetitive outputs: val step 0 = 1%, val step 50 = 13.7%, val step 100 = 45.1% - massive increase
6. Outputs with \boxed{}: val0 = 1245/1319, val 50 = 1001/1319, val 100 = 767/1319 - model losing format
7. Wrong answers without \boxed{}: increasing sharply at step 100

Let me now look at a few more things:
1. The reward function to understand if there's any issue
2. The GRPO config details - especially the KL configuration
3. The data preprocessing to verify the ground truth format
4. Whether there's a reward hacking pattern

The KL_LOSS_COEF=0.001 with kl_loss_type=low_var_kl - this is a KL penalty in the loss, not adaptive. The KL loss went from 0.0026 to 0.29, but ppo_kl stayed small (0.001-0.005).

Wait - the KL in the loss is based on the reference model, not the rollout model. The kl_loss grew100x while ppo_kl (which is the rollout vs current actor KL) stayed at 0.001-0.005. This means the current actor has diverged substantially from the reference model (large kl_loss), but the current actor is close to the rollout policy (small ppo_kl is expected in on-policy PPO).

The GRPO run has:
- algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=False - KL not added to reward
- actor.use_kl_loss=True with kl_loss_coef=0.001 - KL added as loss term

The actor has diverged massively from the reference policy. The entropy explosion (0.35 → 0.86 at step 97) and the 45% repetitive outputs at val step 100 suggest entropy collapse into repetition loops or a more chaotic policy.

Wait, actually high entropy usually means the model is more random/uncertain. But 45% repetitive outputs seem contradictory - repetition loops in LLMs often come from degenerate policies that are confident in certain token patterns (low entropy locally). Let me think about this...

Actually, looking more carefully:
- Steps 1-50: entropy DROPS from 0.35 to ~0.15 (model learns more deterministic correct paths)
- Steps 50-100: entropy RISES sharply from ~0.25 back to ~0.86 (model unlearns or becomes chaotic)

The increase in entropy is consistent with the model drifting away from its original distribution (large KL) and generating increasingly incoherent outputs - repetition loops are actually low-entropy locally (the model keeps outputting the same phrase) but if the loops contain different phrases for different problems, the aggregate entropy might be high.

Actually, wait - model entropy here is computed over token probabilities, not the sentence level. Repetition loops could appear as entropy collapse (the model is very sure about the next token) or as high entropy if the repetitive segments themselves are complex.

Let me look at the actual KL configuration more carefully. The key question is: why did the model collapse after step 20-30?

"""
Preprocess the GSM8k dataset to parquet format
"""

import argparse
import os
import re

import datasets

from verl.utils.hdfs_io import copy, makedirs


def extract_solution(solution_str):
    solution = re.search("#### (\\-?[0-9\\.\\,]+)", solution_str)
    assert solution is not None
    final_solution = solution.group(0)
    final_solution = final_solution.split("#### ")[1].replace(",", "")
    return final_solution


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--local_dir", default=None, help="The save directory for the preprocessed dataset.")
    parser.add_argument("--hdfs_dir", default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--local_dataset_path", default=None, help="The local path to the raw dataset, if it exists.")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--local_save_dir", default="~/data/gsm8k", help="The save directory for the preprocessed dataset."
    )

    args = parser.parse_args()
    local_dataset_path = args.local_dataset_path

    data_source = "openai/gsm8k"

    if local_dataset_path is not None:
        dataset = datasets.load_dataset(local_dataset_path, "main")
    else:
        dataset = datasets.load_dataset(data_source, "main")

    train_dataset = dataset["train"]
    test_dataset = dataset["test"]

    instruction_following = "Let's think step by step and output the final answer within \\boxed{}."

    # add a row to each data item that represents a unique id
    def make_map_fn(split):
        def process_fn(example, idx):
            question_raw = example.pop("question")

            question = question_raw + " " + instruction_following

            answer_raw = example.pop("answer")
            solution = extract_solution(answer_raw)
            data = {
                "data_source": data_source,
                "prompt": [
                    {
                        "role": "user",
                        "content": question,
                    }
                ],
                "ability": "math",
                "reward_model": {"style": "rule", "ground_truth": solution},
                "extra_info": {
                    "split": split,
                    "index": idx,
                    "answer": answer_raw,
                    "question": question_raw,
                },
            }
            return data

        return process_fn

    train_dataset = train_dataset.map(function=make_map_fn("train"), with_indices=True)
    test_dataset = test_dataset.map(function=make_map_fn("test"), with_indices=True)

    hdfs_dir = args.hdfs_dir
    local_save_dir = args.local_dir
    if local_save_dir is not None:
        print("Warning: Argument 'local_dir' is deprecated. Please use 'local_save_dir' instead.")
    else:
        local_save_dir = args.local_save_dir

    train_dataset.to_parquet(os.path.join(local_save_dir, "train.parquet"))
    test_dataset.to_parquet(os.path.join(local_save_dir, "test.parquet"))

    if hdfs_dir is not None:
        makedirs(hdfs_dir)

        copy(src=local_save_dir, dst=hdfs_dir)

import multiprocessing
import threading
from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
from concurrent.futures import TimeoutError as FuturesTimeoutError

try:
    from math_verify.errors import TimeoutException
except ImportError:

    class TimeoutException(Exception):
        pass

    print("To use Math-Verify, please install it first by running `pip install math-verify`.")

_pool = None
_pool_lock = threading.Lock()


def _get_pool():
    global _pool
    if _pool is None:
        with _pool_lock:
            if _pool is None:
                _pool = ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=4, mp_context=multiprocessing.get_context("spawn"))
    return _pool


def _verify_in_subprocess(ground_truth_boxed: str, model_output: str) -> float:
    """Run math_verify in a subprocess where signal.alarm() works."""
    from math_verify.grader import verify
    from math_verify.parser import ExprExtractionConfig, LatexExtractionConfig, parse

    gold_targets = (LatexExtractionConfig(),)
    pred_targets = (ExprExtractionConfig(), LatexExtractionConfig())

    extracted_gold = parse(ground_truth_boxed, gold_targets)
    extracted_pred = parse(model_output, pred_targets)
    if extracted_gold and extracted_pred:
        return max(1.0 if any(verify(g, p) for g in extracted_gold) else 0.0 for p in extracted_pred)
    return 0.0


def compute_score(model_output: str, ground_truth: str, timeout_score: float = 0, timeout: float = 30.0) -> float:
    ret_score = 0.0
    ground_truth_boxed = "\\boxed{" + ground_truth + "}"
    try:
        future = _get_pool().submit(_verify_in_subprocess, ground_truth_boxed, model_output)
        ret_score = future.result(timeout=timeout)
    except (FuturesTimeoutError, TimeoutException):
        ret_score = timeout_score
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error in math_verify compute_score: {e}")
    return ret_score

import json

# Verify the causal chain: 
# 1. Response length grows → clip_ratio rises → more truncated responses
# 2. Truncated responses lose \boxed{} → reward=0 → GRPO penalizes long outputs
# 3. BUT entropy is also rising, suggesting policy is drifting
#
# Let's check: for truncated responses (at max length), what's the reward?
for rstep in ['1','50','100']:
    path = f'/workspace/results/run100/rollouts/{rstep}.jsonl'
    rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open(path)]
    
    # Responses at max length = truncated
    # MAX_RESPONSE_LENGTH=512 tokens, so look at char lengths
    # Need to estimate token count - roughly 3-4 chars per token for English
    # But we see response_length/max: 512.0 tokens in metrics, so the JSONL output
    # is in characters. At step 100, mean=366 tokens, max=512 tokens.
    # The char lengths we see in JSONL are the actual character strings.
    
    # Let's classify: likely truncated if output doesn't end with \boxed{...}
    # and is long
    all_lens = [len(r['output']) for r in rows]
    max_len = max(all_lens)
    threshold = max_len * 0.95  # near max = truncated
    
    truncated = [r for r in rows if len(r['output']) >= threshold]
    trunc_correct = sum(1 for r in truncated if float(r['score']) >= 1.0)
    trunc_has_box = sum(1 for r in truncated if '\\boxed{' in r['output'])
    
    all_correct = sum(1 for r in rows if float(r['score']) >= 1.0)
    all_box = sum(1 for r in rows if '\\boxed{' in r['output'])
    
    print(f"\nRollout step {rstep}:")
    print(f"  max_char_len={max_len}, threshold={threshold:.0f}")
    print(f"  near-max (truncated): {len(truncated)}/{len(rows)} ({100*len(truncated)/len(rows):.1f}%)")
    print(f"  trunc correct: {trunc_correct}/{len(truncated)} ({100*trunc_correct/max(1,len(truncated)):.1f}%)")
    print(f"  trunc has_box: {trunc_has_box}/{len(truncated)} ({100*trunc_has_box/max(1,len(truncated)):.1f}%)")
    print(f"  overall correct: {all_correct}/{len(rows)} ({100*all_correct/len(rows):.1f}%)")
    print(f"  overall has_box: {all_box}/{len(rows)} ({100*all_box/len(rows):.1f}%)")

# Let's count how many val step 100 outputs end without \boxed{} because they're too long.

wrong_box_wrong = [r for r in wrong if '\\boxed{' in r['output']]

# How many val step 100 outputs are very long (likely truncated at token limit)?
for threshold in [1500, 1800, 2000]:

steps.reasoning_content:
Now I have a comprehensive picture of thisRL training run. Let me synthesize all findings into a clear diagnosis before writing the final report.

**Summary of findings:**

**Verdict: Unhealthy** — The run ended below its own baseline on the held-out set.

**Key observations:**

1. **Val accuracy trajectory**: Baseline0.3912 → peak 0.4936 at step 20→ monotonic decline →0.3874 at step 100 (below baseline). This is a clear net regression.

2. **Root cause 1: Insufficient KL regularization allowing policy divergence**
   - `kl_loss_coef=0.001` is very small for a 0.5B model on GRPO
   - `use_kl_in_reward=False` means the KL penalty is only in the loss, not the reward shaping
   - `entropy_coeff=0` means no entropy bonus to prevent collapse
   - KL loss grew113× from 0.00256 → 0.29 (step 1 → 99), while the coefficient stayed fixed at 0.001
   - The actual KL penalty contribution to total loss remained tiny (~0.00029) even as the actor diverged massively from the reference policy
   - ppo_kl (rollout vs updated actor) stayed small (0.001-0.005) — this is healthy, the on-policy constraint works. But the reference-policy KL spiraled.

3. **Root cause 2: Response length growth → truncation cascade**
   - MAX_RESPONSE_LENGTH=512 tokens
   - Clip ratio grew from 6.6% (step 1) → 44.1% (step 99)
   - As the model diverged from reference (entropy rising), it began generating longer outputs and repetition loops
   - Truncated responses are cut off before the `\boxed{}` delimiter → reward = 0
   - This creates a feedback loop: truncated long responses get0 reward, GRPO disadvantages them, but the policy continues to generate long repetitive outputs as KL divergence grows

4. **Manifestation in val generations**:
   - Repetitive outputs: 1.0% → 45.1% (step 0 → 100)
   - Wrong answers without `\boxed{}`: 8.6% → 64.6% (the answer is in the incomplete/truncated reasoning, not formatted correctly)
   - Wrong answers at step 0 mostly had the correct format but wrong value (91.4% had `\boxed{}`)
   - Wrong answers at step 100 mostly lack `\boxed{}` entirely (64.6%) — the model fails to reach the conclusion before truncation or loops indefinitely

5. **Causal chain**:
   - Weak KL regularization (coef=0.001, no reward KL, no entropy bonus) → actor allowed to diverge significantly from reference
   - Policy divergence → entropy explosion (0.35 → 0.80) starting around step 50
   - Entropy explosion → increasingly long/repetitive generation (clip_ratio 6% → 44%)
   - Long/repetitive responses truncated at512 tokens → loss of `\boxed{}` format → reward = 0
   - Training signal degrades as more responses are uniformly penalized for format failure rather than reasoning failure
   - Val accuracy collapses: step 70 hit0.3730 (below baseline), briefly recovers, ends at 0.3874 (below baseline)

6. **Is this a training signal / reward bug?** No — math_verify was installed (v0.9.0 confirmed in wandb requirements.txt), rewards show clean 0.0/1.0 binary signals, no NaN/inf in any metric.

7. **Is this truncated logs?** No — the run completed fully (RUN_EXIT 0), all 100 steps logged, all 11 val evaluations present.

**Root causes (distinguish from symptoms):**

*Root causes:*
1. **KL regularization too weak**: `kl_loss_coef=0.001` with `use_kl_in_reward=False` and `entropy_coeff=0` provides insufficient constraint on policy divergence for a small 0.5B model trained with GRPO at this step budget. The reference-model KL loss grew 113× over training while the coefficient remained fixed.

2. **Response length budget mismatch**: `MAX_RESPONSE_LENGTH=512` tokens is tight for step-by-step GSM8K reasoning. As the policy diverges and generates more verbose/repetitive text, the 512-token ceiling causes an accelerating truncation cascade —37–44% of rollout responses are truncated in the final 10 steps, and truncated responses score 0 regardless of whether the underlying reasoning is correct.

*Symptoms:*
- Entropy explosion (0.35 → 0.86)
- Repetition loops (1% → 45% of val outputs)
- Loss of `\boxed{}` format (wrong answers without `\boxed{}` rose from 8.6% to 64.6%)
- Val accuracy degradation below baseline

arguments.content:
# RL Training Run Diagnosis

## Verdict: Unhealthy

The run ended below its own pre-training baseline. Held-out accuracy peaked at **0.4936 (step 20)**, declined monotonically from step 30 onward, and finished at **0.3874 (step 100)** — 0.4% below the step-0 baseline of 0.3912. The run completed normally (RUN_EXIT 0, no NaN/inf in any logged metric), so the degradation is causal, not an artifact of truncation or instrumentation failure.

---

## Root Causes

### 1. KL regularization is too weak to prevent policy divergence

The launch script sets `kl_loss_coef=0.001`, `use_kl_in_reward=False`, and `entropy_coeff=0`. These three settings together mean the only constraint on how far the actor can drift from the reference policy is a fixed-coefficient KL loss term in the actor objective. There is no KL signal in the reward, no entropy bonus, and no adaptive KL controller.

For Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct trained with GRPO at this scale, 0.001 is not enough. The reference-policy KL loss grew from **0.00256 at step 1 to 0.29008 at step 99 — a 113× increase** — while the coefficient stayed fixed at 0.001, meaning the actual KL penalty contribution to the total loss stayed negligible throughout. The ppo-KL (between the rollout policy and the updated actor, the on-policy constraint) remained healthy at 0.001–0.005 throughout, which confirms the per-step update size is fine: the divergence is cumulative drift away from the reference, not within-step instability.

### 2. A 512-token response ceiling creates an accelerating truncation cascade once the policy drifts

`MAX_RESPONSE_LENGTH=512` was sufficient early in training: at step 1, only **6.6% of rollout responses hit the ceiling**. As the policy diverged from the reference, it began generating more verbose and repetitive outputs. The response clip ratio rose steadily — crossing 10% at step 22, 20% at step 50, 30% at step 53 — reaching **44.1% at step 99**. At the final training step the mean response length was 366 tokens (up from ~302 at step 1) with the max at exactly 512.

Truncated responses never reach the `\boxed{}` delimiter that `math_verify.compute_score` requires, so they receive reward 0 regardless of whether the underlying reasoning is correct. This amplifies the KL-divergence problem: the feedback signal for long outputs is uniformly zero, which does not teach the model to reason more concisely — instead it destabilizes GRPO's advantage estimates.

---

## Causal Chain

1. **Weak KL regularization** allows the actor to diverge continuously from the reference model across 100 steps. The 113× growth in KL loss is the direct measurement of this drift.

2. **Policy drift causes entropy to explode**. Entropy dropped initially (0.35 → 0.15, steps 1–44) as the model learned the task, then rose sharply (0.15 → 0.86 by step 99) as the policy left the region of the reference model it was initialized near. Rising entropy in an autoregressive LM correlates with more diffuse, repetitive, and incoherent outputs.

3. **Long/repetitive outputs collide with the 512-token ceiling**. Repetitive outputs in held-out val_generations grew from **1.0% at step 0 to 45.1% at step 100**. Many of these loop on a sub-problem statement without ever issuing a final boxed answer.

4. **Truncation strips the `\boxed{}` format, converting correct-but-unfinished reasoning into reward-0 responses**. At val step 0, 91.4% of wrong answers still contained `\boxed{}` (wrong value, not missing format). At val step 100, **64.6% of wrong answers had no `\boxed{}` at all** — the model failed to reach the answer line before truncation or entered a repetition loop. The mean output length of wrong answers grew from 1067 chars at step 0 to 1558 chars at step 100, while correct answers stayed around 903–969 chars.

5. **Val accuracy collapses below baseline**. Steps 60–100 are all below the step-10 high-water mark; step 70 (0.3730) and step 100 (0.3874) are both below the untrained baseline of 0.3912.

---

## Distinguishing Root Causes from Symptoms

| | Evidence |
|---|---|
| **Root cause — weak KL regularization** | `kl_loss_coef=0.001`, `use_kl_in_reward=False`, `entropy_coeff=0`; KL loss ×113 over run; ppo-KL healthy (rules out per-step instability) |
| **Root cause — 512-token ceiling too tight** | Clip ratio 6.6% → 44.1%; mean response length grows monotonically; truncated responses score 0 regardless of reasoning quality |
| *Symptom* — entropy explosion | Follows from reference-policy divergence, not an independent cause |
| *Symptom* — repetition loops | Consequence of entropy explosion and policy drift |
| *Symptom* — loss of `\boxed{}` format | Consequence of truncation and repetition, not a reward-function bug |
| *Symptom* — val accuracy below baseline | Net result of the above chain |

The reward function itself (`math_verify` v0.9.0, confirmed installed from wandb `requirements.txt`) worked correctly throughout: rewards are clean binary 0/1 values with no NaN or scoring errors in the log.

**Root cause 1 — KL regularization too weak.** The launch config sets `kl_loss_coef=0.001`, `use_kl_in_reward=False`, and `entropy_coeff=0`. Responses truncated at 512 tokens never reach the `\boxed{}` delimiter that `math_verify` requires, so they score 0 regardless of whether the underlying reasoning is correct.

- Weak KL constraint → actor diverges from reference (KL loss ×113).
